name: Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle
purpose: To help astronauts explore more of the Moon by providing battery-powered transportation across the lunar surface.
discoveries: Helped astronauts explore the Hadley-Apennine region.
Allowed astronauts to travel approximately 17.5 miles across the lunar surface
Supported the collection of lunar rocks and soil for scientific study.
facts: It was the first vehicle driven by humans on the Moon.
It had four wheels and ran on batteries.
Astronauts David Scott and James Irwin used it during Apollo 15.
scientificImpact: Helped astronauts investigate the Hadley-Apennine region and collect lunar rocks and soil, including samples that improved our understanding of the Moon's geological history.
hardwareLocation: Hadley-Apennine region, Moon (left parked near the Apollo 15 landing site).
hardwareStory: A battery-powered, four-wheeled vehicle that allowed astronauts David Scott and James Irwin to travel farther across the Moon during their Apollo 15 exploration.

name: Sojourner
purpose: To explore the Martian surface, study rocks and soil, and demonstrate that a small robotic rover could operate on another planet.
discoveries: Studied the chemical composition of Martian rocks and soil.
Returned images of the Martian landscape.
Provided information about the Martian environment.
facts: It was NASA's first rover to operate on Mars.
It was about the size of a microwave oven.
It worked for 83 days, much longer than its planned seven-day mission.
scientificImpact: Analyzed rocks and soil at 16 locations and helped demonstrate that robotic rovers could successfully explore another planet.
hardwareLocation: Ares Vallis, Mars (Mars Pathfinder landing site).
hardwareStory: A lightweight, six-wheeled rover deployed from the Mars Pathfinder lander. It drove around the landing site, photographed the terrain, and examined nearby rocks.

name: Spirit
purpose: To explore Martian rocks and soil and investigate whether water once existed on Mars.
discoveries: Found strong evidence that Mars was once much wetter.
Studied rocks and minerals that provided clues about ancient water.
Explored the Martian surface for more than six years.
facts: Spirit had a twin rover named Opportunity.
It operated for more than six years.
It travelled approximately 4.8 miles across Mars.
scientificImpact: Found geological evidence that water had altered rocks and soils on ancient Mars, helping scientists understand the planet's wetter past.
hardwareLocation: Gusev Crater, Mars (last resting area near the Troy region).
hardwareStory: One of NASA's twin Mars Exploration Rovers. Spirit explored Gusev Crater, investigated rocks and soil, and travelled across the Martian landscape for more than six years.

name: Opportunity
purpose: To study Martian rocks and soil and investigate whether ancient Mars had conditions that could support microbial life.
discoveries: Found evidence that liquid water once existed on Mars.
Studied rocks showing signs of past water activity.
Helped scientists understand the history of water on Mars.
facts: Its twin rover was named Spirit.
It worked for almost 15 years.
It travelled more than 28 miles across Mars.
scientificImpact: Found strong geological evidence that liquid water once existed on Mars and operated for almost 15 years, far exceeding its planned mission.
hardwareLocation: Perseverance Valley, western rim of Endeavour Crater, Mars (last known location).
hardwareStory: Spirit's twin rover explored Meridiani Planum, travelling between craters and examining rocks that preserved clues about ancient water.

name: Curiosity
purpose: To investigate whether ancient Mars had environmental conditions that could support microbial life.
discoveries: Found evidence of ancient freshwater environments.
Discovered chemical and mineral evidence of past habitable environments.
Studied rocks that preserve clues about ancient Martian environments.
facts: Curiosity is about the size of a small car.
It landed inside Gale Crater.
It uses a robotic arm to study Martian rocks and soil.
scientificImpact: Discovered evidence of ancient freshwater environments and chemical conditions that could once have supported microbial life.
hardwareLocation: Gale Crater and Mount Sharp, Mars (active exploration area).
hardwareStory: A car-sized mobile science laboratory that uses cameras, a robotic arm, a drill, and onboard instruments to investigate Martian rocks and soil.

name: Perseverance
purpose: To search for signs of ancient microbial life, study Martian geology, and collect rock and soil samples for possible future return to Earth.
discoveries: Collected rock samples for possible future scientific study on Earth.
Investigated ancient environments in Jezero Crater.
Studied rocks and minerals that help scientists understand the history of Mars.
facts: Perseverance has a robotic arm for examining rocks.
It carries a device called MOXIE that demonstrated oxygen production from the Martian atmosphere.
It carried the Ingenuity helicopter to Mars.
scientificImpact: Investigates an ancient Martian lake and river delta, preserves rock samples for future study, and has identified a potential biosignature that requires further investigation.
hardwareStory: A mobile science laboratory exploring Jezero Crater. It studies rocks, searches for signs of ancient microbial life, and collects and seals samples for possible future return.

name: Ingenuity
purpose: To demonstrate that powered, controlled flight was possible in the thin atmosphere of Mars.
discoveries: Demonstrated the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.
Completed 72 successful flights.
Provided valuable information about flying in the Martian atmosphere.
facts: Ingenuity was a small robotic helicopter.
Its first flight took place on April 19, 2021.
It was originally designed for just five test flights but completed 72.
scientificImpact: Completed 72 flights, proving that powered flight is possible on another planet and demonstrating how aerial vehicles could support future exploration.
hardwareLocation: Jezero Crater, Mars (grounded after its final flight in January 2024).
hardwareStory: A small autonomous helicopter delivered to Mars with Perseverance. It demonstrated powered, controlled flight in the planet's extremely thin atmosphere.

name: Voyager 1
purpose: To explore the outer planets and investigate the space beyond the Sun's protective bubble, known as the heliosphere.
discoveries: Discovered new moons around Jupiter and Saturn.
Helped scientists study the outer planets.
Became the first human-made spacecraft to enter interstellar space.
facts: Voyager 1 launched in 1977.
It carries a Golden Record containing sounds and images from Earth.
It entered interstellar space in August 2012.
scientificImpact: Returned discoveries about Jupiter and Saturn and continues to provide measurements that help scientists investigate the environment between the stars.
hardwareLocation: Interstellar space, beyond the heliosphere (still travelling and communicating with Earth).
hardwareStory: A spacecraft launched in 1977 to explore the outer planets. After its encounters with Jupiter and Saturn, it continued travelling beyond the Sun's heliosphere.
